coordinates_and_metric: Euclidean complex frequency space; z=xi+i*eta, real volume dxi*deta. Dot products in exponentials are bilinear.

first_figure.density_normalization: g_sigma integrates to1; actual test integral represents D^r delta0, D=-i*d/dx.
first_figure.left_slice: eta=0, q=xi/t; weighted energy divided by g_sigma(0)^2/(4*pi^2)*t^(2r-8) is q^(2r)/(1+q^2)^4
first_figure.eta_samples: 900 samples over[-5,5]; entire Gaussian profiles exist beyond plotted interval
first_figure.full_surface_example: For n=2,P=z1,N={z1=0},parameter z2=xi2+i*eta2, induced dS=dxi2*deta2. U=z2^3*g1(eta2)/(2*pi), producing1_x1 tensor D2^3 delta0.

second_figure.left_domain: Displayed x in[-1,1]; all three kernels solve(D-i)^3 u=0 globally.
second_figure.left_characteristic_measure: N={i}, counting measure, tau=1, amplitudes a=0,1,2
second_figure.right_domain: X=(-1,1)^2; only x2 coordinate and derivative order shown.
second_figure.infinite_scope: a_l=1-2^(-l), l>=1, locally finite on X; plotted seven terms are numerical samples, not the complete distribution. Boundary1 is outside X.
second_figure.homogeneous_operator: P(z)=z1, P(D)=D1, all local orders preserved.

authorship: GPT-6.1 Sol (OpenAI), Ultra; original exact scientific plots; CC0 1.0
human_source: Lars Hormander, The Analysis of Linear Partial Differential Operators II, two unnumbered representation exercises on printedp300.
